title: DONJ Jewellery: Medusa + Next.js Headless Rebuild with a 100K+ Diamond Marketplace & Custom Ring Builder

archive.excerpt: A full ecommerce rebuild for DONJ Jewellery, replacing the legacy WordPress and WooCommerce storefront with a modular headless platform using Medusa v2 and Next.js 16.

seo.title: DONJ Jewellery Headless Commerce Case Study | Dynamic Dreamz
seo.description: See how Dynamic Dreamz redesigned Don J's website into a luxury jewelry platform, with a dynamic ring browsing experience, real-time preview & boosted sales.

challenge.heading: The Challenge
challenge.description: DONJ's original WordPress and WooCommerce storefront still functioned, but the architecture had accumulated performance, pricing, content and integration constraints. The rebuild needed to solve the underlying commerce system—not simply redesign the interface.

items.description: The monolithic WordPress + WooCommerce storefront suffered from slow page loads, plugin conflicts and limited scalability.
The PHP / jQuery engagement-ring builder had become difficult to maintain and was prone to pricing bugs.
The diamond feed was hardcoded inside templates, making supplier changes and lab-grown expansion difficult.
The store operated in CAD while the live diamond feed priced in USD, creating a complex multi-currency pricing problem.
High-ticket ring purchases had no deposit or partial-payment workflow.
Marketing depended on developers for homepage and content updates.
Frontend and backend pricing could drift, creating a trust problem when displayed and charged prices did not match.
The legacy architecture lacked server-side rendering, strong Core Web Vitals and structured-data support.

solutions.heading: How We Rebuilt the Commerce Platform
solutions.lead: Next.js 16 renders the customer-facing storefront while Medusa v2 owns commerce logic, pricing and integrations. This separation gave DONJ a modular platform without allowing different parts of the stack to calculate independent prices. Product configuration, currency conversion, upgrades, cart totals and payment amounts all resolve back to the same backend authority.

items.text: Replatformed the storefront from WordPress + WooCommerce to a headless Next.js 16 frontend with Medusa v2 as the commerce backend.
Made Medusa the single pricing authority so the display price, cart price, order price and gateway charge resolve from the same backend logic.
Integrated PostgreSQL, Nivoda, Algolia, Converge and PayPal as independent services around a modular commerce core.
Built custom commerce modules for the engagement-ring builder, deposit schedules, upgrades, customer accounts and live diamond purchasing.
Separated content from the old WordPress runtime using Gutenberg-style blocks rendered by typed React components.
Introduced a layered caching and search architecture so the 100K+ diamond catalog could be browsed and filtered quickly.

items.title: Engagement Ring Builder
items.description: Customers design a ring in three steps: select a diamond from the live Nivoda feed, choose a setting by metal and style, then review the configuration, add upgrades and check out. A single backend price-derivation function applies discounts, converts the USD diamond price at the locked exchange rate and returns one whole-dollar total.

items.title: 100K+ Diamond Marketplace
items.description: A scheduled job imports more than 100,000 Nivoda stones into Medusa with certificate numbers, measurements and delivery data. Shoppers can filter by shape, carat, color, clarity and cut, view GIA / IGI certificates and 360° media, compare stones and then move a selected diamond into the ring builder.

items.title: Multi-Currency, Whole-Dollar Pricing
items.description: The store base currency is CAD while the diamond feed prices in USD. Exchange rates are cached server-side for one hour. Ring pricing, diamond conversion and upgrade calculations are rounded consistently so values do not drift between storefront and checkout.

items.title: Deposit & Partial Payment Plans
items.description: For high-ticket orders, a custom Medusa module splits the order into whole-dollar installments. Each installment is floored and the final payment absorbs the rounding remainder so the schedule always adds back to the exact order total.

items.title: Converge + PayPal Payments
items.description: Converge hosted Lightbox handles Canadian cards while keeping card data away from DONJ's servers. PayPal supports international shoppers and returning-customer vaulting. Both gateways use the backend-calculated order amount.

items.title: CMS Blocks & Marketing Autonomy
items.description: Content lives in Medusa through Gutenberg-style blocks and is rendered by typed React components. Hero banners, product grids, trust content and educational modules can publish without the previous WordPress runtime or routine developer involvement.

items.title: Wishlist & Customer Accounts
items.description: Logged-in wishlists persist and sync across devices while guests receive a session-based version. Customer accounts include order history, addresses, deposit schedules with pay-now actions and support for transferring an order between accounts for gifting.

items.title: Ring Upgrades
items.description: Engraving, rush delivery, insurance and gift packaging are priced as percentages of the effective ring price. Grouped upgrades are mutually exclusive where required, and the same pricing logic is used across frontend and backend.

items.title: Algolia Search & Discovery
items.description: Products, diamonds and categories are indexed nightly into Algolia, powering autocomplete, faceted filtering and 'did you mean' suggestions across category and diamond discovery experiences.

items.title: Transactional Email & Reminders
items.description: Resend sends order confirmations, shipping updates and deposit reminders using custom MJML templates, with scheduled jobs tracking which reminders have already been delivered.

projectDelivery.heading: Backend as the Single Pricing Authority

customSections.heading: Backend as the Single Pricing Authority
customSections.lead: Nothing prices a product independently on the storefront. Next.js presents the experience; Medusa controls commerce logic and communicates with the database, payment gateways, diamond supplier and search layer.
customSections.description: Core rule: Display price = cart price = order price = gateway charge.

customSections.heading: Fixing the Infrastructure Beneath the Storefront
customSections.lead: The legacy diamond experience called Nivoda directly on every request. With more than 100,000 stones, filters could take 8–15 seconds. The new architecture introduced layered caching and a dedicated search index, while the security model moved away from years of plugin-driven risk.
customSections.description: Result documented in the source: the diamond filter page loads in under 800ms at p95, with subsequent filters hitting Algolia at roughly 150ms.

customSections.heading: What Changed After the Rebuild
customSections.lead: The project produced measurable improvements across speed, mobile conversion, pricing accuracy, high-ticket payment flexibility and marketing autonomy.

customSections.heading: A Cross-Functional Delivery Team
customSections.lead: Every currency and rounding decision was logged in a running DECISIONS.md before development. Backend modules and APIs were implemented first, followed by frontend features, visual regression testing, staging UAT against real Converge and PayPal sandboxes, and then production release.

customSections.heading: Headless was not the goal. Reliable commerce was.
takeaways: The platform evolved through documented decisions, one shared pricing authority and a focus on whole-dollar accuracy. The architecture is modular enough to change payment providers, diamond suppliers or CMS components without rewriting the commerce core.
Marketing owns content. Engineering owns correctness. Customers get one consistent experience from a lower-ticket jewellery purchase through a high-value custom engagement ring.
Because in jewellery, even a one-dollar pricing mismatch can become a broken promise.

challenge.heading: Challenges
challenge.description: Evrgreen had a disruptive idea, a clear audience, and a brand full of warmth and personality. What they needed was a technical foundation sophisticated enough to power a rental and subscription business on a platform that doesn’t natively support either.

items.title: Shopify doesn’t natively support rental models
items.description: Shopify is built for standard eCommerce products that are sold, not rented. Building a fully functional rental solution on Shopify required engineering bespoke systems from scratch, with no off-the-shelf solution available.

items.title: Event-based shopping with cross-collection flexibility
items.description: Customers needed to shop by event Halloween, Christmas, 4th of July, New Year while also being able to freely mix items from multiple event collections into a single rental box. The standard Shopify collection architecture doesn’t support this kind of cross-collection, persistent-cart behaviour.

items.title: Persistent box state across the entire site
items.description: The active box configuration, box type, rental duration, and start and end dates needed to persist across every page of the site until checkout or reset, regardless of which collections or pages the customer visited. This required a custom application layer to manage and maintain.

items.title: Fixed box pricing with dynamic discounting
items.description: Evrgreen’s pricing model is fixed per box tier, not per item. No matter which individual products a customer adds to their box, the final total always equals the fixed box price. Engineering dynamic, per-product discounting that automatically adjusts behind the scenes to maintain this fixed total was a significant technical challenge.

solutions.heading: Solution
solutions.lead: Dynamic Dreamz approached the Evrgreen project as a platform engineering challenge, designing and building an entirely custom Shopify application layer that powered every aspect of the rental and subscription experience, alongside a beautifully customised Stretch theme storefront that made it all feel effortless.
